goal: Reduce peak GPU allocated memory for one complete offline image batch inference, preserving the source quality checks and throughput constraint.
completion: The workload is exactly one complete offline batch inference: infer(model, pixels) at resnet_inference.py:14-16, i.e. ResNetForImageClassification forward model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode() on the FP32 NCHW batch=32 tensor built at resnet_inference.py:29 from assets pixels.npy as images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % len(images)].contiguous(). Completion is the returned full logits tensor (shape [32, 1000]) with all GPU work finished: the source times each repeat between torch.cuda.synchronize() calls (resnet_inference.py:42,46), so the completion boundary is the post-forward CUDA synchronization. Excluded from the measured invocation: model loading, pixels.npy host load and H2D transfer, batch-index construction, reference construction and quality checks, reference .pt save, warmup, the statistical repeats harness, result.json writing, and the opt-in --profile diagnostic trace.
state_protocol: prepare(context, request): applies the source's configure() numerical policy (num_threads=4, num_interop_threads=1, manual_seed(20261020), TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark off, float32_matmul_precision 'highest') with torch.cuda.set_device(context['device']); loads ResNetForImageClassification from the assets directory (dirname of request assets model_config, which also contains model.safetensors, preprocessor_config.json, pixels.npy) with local_files_only=True and dtype=torch.float32, moves it to context['device'] and sets .eval(); loads pixels.npy to the device and pre-builds the frozen batch=32 input pixels = images[torch.arange(32) % len(images)].contiguous() exactly as resnet_inference.py:29. Model and input stay GPU-resident in state; nothing is loaded at import time and CUDA is not initialized at import time. reset(state): restores the deterministic starting point outside timing by re-asserting model.eval() and torch.manual_seed(20261020) and clearing the recorded peak; the forward itself is stateless (torch.inference_mode, no grads, no caches since cudnn.benchmark is off), so no further mutable state exists and the process group is untouched. run(state): resets CUDA peak memory stats (the source's per-repeat reset at resnet_inference.py:43), executes the single forward under torch.inference_mode() annotated with the 'forward' discovery phase, records torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() (the source's peak read at resnet_inference.py:48), and returns the full logits tensor. observe(state, result): returns detached CPU copies of the complete [32, 1000] logits and the argmax predicted class ids; no timings or performance counters. metrics(state, result, elapsed_ms): reports peak_allocated_bytes from the recorded CUDA allocator peak for the forward, images_per_second = batch * 1000 / elapsed_ms matching the source's batch * 1e9 / elapsed_ns, plus latency_ms and batch size; no fabricated values. models(state): exposes the loaded root model under key 'model' for discovery and controlled replacement; no operator groups or optimization targets are preselected.
invariants: Model is microsoft/resnet-18 loaded from the local assets directory via ResNetForImageClassification.from_pretrained(local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32), kept in eval mode on context['device']; weights come from assets model.safetensors with no downloads.

Numerical policy frozen from common.py configure(): torch.float32, torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.set_num_threads(4), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1), torch.manual_seed(20261020).

Input tensor frozen: FP32 NCHW batch=32 built once from pixels.npy (3 real preprocessed images) as images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % 3].contiguous(); batch size, image data and tensor layout must not change.

The measured workload is the single forward model(pixel_values=pixels).logits executed under torch.inference_mode(); the full work amount must be preserved even though the objective targets peak memory.

peak_allocated_bytes is the per-process PyTorch CUDA allocated peak (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() after reset_peak_memory_stats() before the forward and CUDA synchronization at both timing boundaries); it is not whole-GPU, reserved or driver memory.
images_per_second is full-request throughput of the fixed batch=32 forward, batch * 1e9 / elapsed_ns, and must remain >= 0.95 x baseline (objective constraint).

Quality gates from workloads.json resnet_inference.correctness: full 1000-class logits compared with atol=0.0001, rtol=0.0001 (close_check), exact top-1 equality torch.equal(actual.argmax(-1), reference.argmax(-1)) with require_exact_top1=true, and the negative control rejecting a +1 logits corruption.
Observations expose every logit and the predicted class integers as detached tensors; no hash-only or sampled outputs, and no elapsed times or performance counters in correctness observations.

Single-process, single-CUDA-device task on context['device']; no distributed launch, no second reference model on GPU (reference observations are CPU copies), no process-group initialization or destruction.

Timing boundaries follow the source: CUDA synchronization before and after the measured forward; model load, pixel load/H2D, batch construction, checks, warmup and profiling are outside timed execution.
assumptions: The assets directory for from_pretrained is the dirname shared by request assets model_config/model_weights/preprocessor_config/pixels (all under .../validation-assets/resnet18); from_pretrained reads config.json and model.safetensors from that directory, matching the source's --assets usage.
pixels.npy (shape [3, 3, 224, 224], float32, preprocessed real images per asset-manifest) is the actual task data; the batch=32 tensor repeats it via arange % 3 exactly as the source.

The framework performs the warmup=2 / repeats=5 statistical harness and the boundary CUDA synchronizations; the adapter's run() is the single measured invocation whose elapsed_ms yields images_per_second.

Reading torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() right after the forward (before observe/metrics) reproduces the source's peak measurement, since the allocator peak is monotonic from the reset and no other GPU allocation intervenes inside run().
The framework collects reference observations on CPU, so observe() returns CPU copies of the GPU logits; no second reference model is allocated in the worker.
The 'online' batch=1 workload row and the held-out 'unseen_batch' batch=7 row in the source are not part of this frozen request; only the offline batch=32 row is executed.

The opt-in --profile diagnostic (profile_once) and the reference construction/torch.save in the source harness are benchmark scaffolding outside the measured invocation and are not reproduced as work inside run().

request['objective'] declares no source collector descriptor, so metrics() reports the objective directly: the measured CUDA allocated peak and the throughput derived from the unchanged batch=32 work amount.
